 Dated this the 9th day of August, 2024
 Judgment
The appeal has been filed challenging the judgment of the Reference Court in L.A.R. No.480/2010.
An extent of 0.20 Ares of land in Survey No.1755/1 of Vanchiyoor Village in Thiruvananthapuram Taluk was acquired for the widening of Pattoor - Choorakkatupalayam Road.
Section 4(1) notification was published on 21.11.2007.
The award was passed on 06.03.2009 for an amount of 1,50,841/- as compensation.
The land had been taken possession on 20.03.2009.

The Reference Court has, for the reason that the claimant failed to appear or be represented by an Advocate, disposed of the land acquisition reference holding that the compensation appears to be reasonable and the claimants are not entitled to claim compensation.
2. This appeal has been filed by the claimants 1 & 3 before the court below.

It is stated that the 2 nd claimant, who was conducting the case, died and hence necessary instructions could not be given to the counsel, which is the reason why there was no appearance before the Reference Court.

It is pointed out that for 2024:KER:60843 LA.APP. NO. 11 OF 2024 similar acquisitions for the very same purpose, the question of compensation payable had been finally concluded by this Court in the judgments in L.A.A. Nos.284/2012 and 353/2012.

It is pointed out that in L.A.A. No.284/2012, the Court was concerned with acquisition on the basis of Section 4(1) notification which was published on 19.05.2006 for the purpose of widening of Pattoor - Choorakkattupalayam Road.
This Court re-fixed the market value of the land as 23,00,000/- per Are.

In L.A.A. No.353/2012, taking note of the fact that the acquisition was based on Section 4(1) notification published on 24.04.2008,

almost two years after the notification in the case of L.A.A.No.284/2012, this Court re-fixed the value of land at 27,50,000/- per Are.
3.
In the case on hand, the notification was issued on 21.11.2007, which is a few months before the notification involved in L.A.A. No.353/2012.
Going by the same yardstick followed in the two appeals referred above, this Court is of the opinion that the land value can be safely re-fixed at 25,00,000/- per Are.
This appeal is hence allowed.
The land value is re-fixed at 25,00,000/- per Are.

The appellants are eligible for all statutory benefits admissible under Sections 23(2), 23(1)(A) and under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894 on the re-fixed 2024:KER:60843 LA.APP. NO. 11 OF 2024 compensation.
The decree copy shall be issued after ensuring that the entire court fee payable on the appeal memorandum is remitted by the appellants.
The appellants will not be entitled to the interest on the enhanced compensation for the period of 2856 days as ordered on 04.03.2024 in C.M.Appl.No.1 of 2024.
